parts.title: Roller coaster: the great fairground attraction
parts.article:
Roller coaster: the great fairground attraction
 
How they move
(A) Like a passenger train, a roller coaster consists of a series of connected cars that move on a track. But unlike a passenger train, it has no engine or power source of its own. For most of the ride, it is moved only by the forces of inertia and gravity. The only exertion of energy occurs at the very beginning of the ride when the coaster train is pulled up the lift hill.
 
(B) The traditional lifting mechanism is a long length of chain running up the hill under the track. The chain is fastened in a loop, which is wound around a gear at the top of the hill and another one at the bottom. The gear at the bottom of the hill is turned by a motor. This turns the chain so that it continually moves up the hill like a long conveyor belt. The coaster cars grip onto the chain, which simply pulls them to the top. At the summit, the train is released and starts its descent.
 
(C) The purpose of this initial ascent is to build up a sort of reservoir of potential energy, which simply means that as the coaster gets higher in the air, there is a greater distance gravity can pull it down.
 
(D) As the train starts coasting down the hill, this potential energy is converted into kinetic energy (energy of motion), and the train speeds up. At the bottom of the hill, this has reached its maximum, and this propels the train up the second hill, again building up the potential-energy level.
 
(E) In this way, the course of the track is constantly converting energy from kinetic to potential and back again. This fluctuation in acceleration is what makes roller coasters so much fun. At its most basic level, this is all a roller coaster is – a machine that uses gravity and inertia to send a train along a winding track.
 
Coasting through history
(F) Roller coasters have a long, fascinating history. Their direct ancestors were ice slides, popular in Russia in the 16th and 17th centuries. They consisted of a long, steep, wooden slide covered in ice. Riders walked up a ladder or set of stairs to the top of the slide, as high as 21 metres up. At the top, they climbed into sleds made of wood or blocks of ice and shot down the slope. At the base, the sleds would crash-land in a sand pile.
 
(G) It seems that the idea was then imported into France. For most of the year, the warmer climate would melt the ice, so the French started building waxed slides instead. To help the sleds move down these slides, they added wheels, and in 1817, for the first time, a train was attached to the track. The French continued to expand on this idea, coming up with more complex track layouts, with multiple cars and all sorts of twists and turns.
 
(H) The first American roller coaster was built in the mountains of Pennsylvania in the mid-1800s, originally to provide an easy way to send coal to the railway 29 km down the mountain. When the track was first built, a crew at the bottom of the mountain would attach the cart to a team of mules after emptying the load, and the mules would drag it back up to the top. They were eventually replaced with steam engines to make the system more efficient.
 
(I) Soon after these improvements were made, the railway company built a new tunnel that brought the freight trains much closer to the coal mine. No longer required for its original purpose, the roller coaster was configured as a ‘scenic tour’. For one dollar, tourists got a leisurely ride up to the top of the mountain, followed by a wild, bumpy ride straight down. This was soon a resounding success, attracting thousands of tourists every year.
 
(J) Scenic rides like this continued to thrive and were joined by wooden roller coasters similar to the ones we know today. These coasters were the main attraction at popular amusement parks throughout the United States, such as the many parks of Coney Island in New York. By the 1920s, roller coasters were in full swing, with some 2,000 rides in operation around the country.
 
(K) Following the Great Depression, a decline in roller-coaster production began in the early 1930s, but a second roller-coaster boom in the 1970s and the beginning of the 1980s revitalised the amusement-park industry and introduced a slew of innovative tubular steel coasters.
 
(L) This was followed by a decline in interest for the rest of the decade, but since the early 1990s the amusement-park industry has experienced another coaster boom of sorts. New launching techniques and other technological developments have opened up a world of options for designers, so in some rides you feel as if you are flying. In the next few years we can expect to see many faster, taller and more twisted rides popping up in amusement parks around the world.

analyses.content: 看到 "long length" 可能会想填 length，但它修饰的是核心词 chain（链条），这才是提升装置的主体。
(Paragraph B) The traditional lifting mechanism is a long length of chain running up the hill under the track.
题目图中箭头指向沿着轨道上坡的长条状物体，文中明确提到传统的提升装置是一条在轨道下方运行的长链条。
题目图中箭头指向顶部或底部的圆轮状物体，文中提到链条绕在山顶和山底的齿轮上。
注意不要填 loop，loop 是链条原本的状态（环状），而图示指的是链条缠绕的那个具体部件（齿轮）。
(Paragraph B) The chain is fastened in a loop, which is wound around a gear at the top of the hill and another one at the bottom.
题目图中箭头指向底部齿轮旁的驱动方块，文中指出底部的齿轮是由马达转动的。
可能会误填 engine，但这段专门讲的是传统的提升机制（mechanical），文中用词是 motor。
(Paragraph B) The gear at the bottom of the hill is turned by a motor.

groups.contentHtml:
Modern roller coasters are descended from 16th-century Russian slides with a surface of .
In France, because of the higher temperatures, the wooden surface on the slides was , and were attached to the cars to ease the descent.
The first US roller coaster was used for transporting down a mountainside in carts.
Initially, these were pulled by mules, but in time power was produced by .

analyses.content: 这里的 surface of ... 结构在文中完全对应，直接照抄 ice 即可，不需要填 ice slides。
题目问俄罗斯滑梯的表面是什么，文中直接提到它们的表面是冰。
(Paragraph F) Their direct ancestors were ice slides, popular in Russia in the 16th and 17th centuries. They consisted of a long, steep, wooden slide covered in ice. ... with a surface of ice.
题目说在法国因为气温高，木制表面被怎样处理了，文中说法国人开始建造打蜡的滑梯。
这是一个形容词填空，对应文中 waxed slides 中的修饰语，不要填成了 melted（那是冰的状态）。
(Paragraph G) For most of the year, the warmer climate would melt the ice, so the French started building waxed slides instead.
题目说为了减缓下降（其实是帮助移动），车上装了什么，文中提到为了帮助滑板下滑，他们加上了轮子。
题目中的 "attached to the cars" 对应文中的 "added ... "，填名词复数 wheels。
(Paragraph G) To help the sleds move down these slides, they added wheels, and in 1817, for the first time, a train was attached to the track.
(Paragraph H) The first American roller coaster was built ... originally to provide an easy way to send coal to the railway 29 km down the mountain.
可能会注意到 mule（骡子）或 tourists（游客），但题目问的是最初的用途（used for transporting），那是运 coal。
题目问美国第一个过山车是用来运送什么下山的，文中明确说是为了把煤送到铁路。
题目说最初由骡子拉，后来动力由什么产生，文中提到它们最终被蒸汽引擎取代。
题目限制“不超过两个词”，虽然文中出现在句尾，但 steam engines 是完整的动力来源名称。
(Paragraph H) When the track was first built, a crew ... would attach the cart to a team of mules ... They were eventually replaced with steam engines to make the system more efficient.

questions.question: The earliest modifications to the basic slide were made in France.

analyses.content: 题目说最早的改进是在法国进行的，文中提到该点子传入法国后，法国人做出了打蜡、加轮子等改进，符合描述。
虽然俄罗斯是起源，但题目强调的是 "modifications"（修改/改良），这是法国人做的。
(Paragraph G) It seems that the idea was then imported into France... the French started building waxed slides instead... they added wheels... The French continued to expand on this idea...

questions.question: Rollercoasters continued to increase in popularity throughout the 1920s and 1930s.

analyses.content: (Paragraph J & K) By the 1920s, roller coasters were in full swing... Following the Great Depression, a decline in roller-coaster production began in the early 1930s...
题目说在 1920 和 1930 年代持续增长，但文中明确说 1930 年代初就开始衰退了。
看到 1920s 很繁荣可能会想选 True，但必须同时满足 "throughout 1920s and 1930s" 这个时间跨度，30年代的衰退（decline）使得命题错误。

questions.question: New roller-coaster technology was introduced in the 1970s in response to public demand.

analyses.content: 文中确实提到了 1970 年代引入了新技术（钢管过山车），但从未提及这是为了“响应公众需求”。
不要脑补“因为受欢迎所以就是响应需求”，文中只陈述了技术革新这一事实，没有解释其背后的动因是 public demand。
(Paragraph K) ...a second roller-coaster boom in the 1970s and the beginning of the 1980s revitalised the amusement-park industry and introduced a slew of innovative tubular steel coasters.

questions.question: Rollercoasters were less popular for most of the 1980s than in the 1970s and 1990s.

analyses.content: 题目比较受喜爱程度：80年代不如70年代和90年代；文中提到 70年代是热潮，80年代初之后是衰退，90年代初又是热潮，逻辑吻合。
文中句子较长，需理清时间轴：70s Boom -> 80s Decline (rest of the decade) -> 90s Boom。

(Paragraph K & L) ...boom in the 1970s... This was followed by a decline in interest for the rest of the decade [1980s], but since the early 1990s the amusement-park industry has experienced another coaster boom...

questions.question: The design of roller-coaster rides became more varied in the 1990s.

analyses.content: 题目说 1990 年代设计变得更多样化，文中提到新技术为设计师打开了“选择的世界”，意味着选择更多、更丰富。
"Opened up a world of options" 就是 "more varied" 的同义替换。
(Paragraph L) New launching techniques and other technological developments have opened up a world of options for designers...
